notes.text: Overall, this is a deliberately flawed fixture repository designed to trigger static analysis findings. The most severe real issues are: (1) command injection in index.js:13, (2) eval() in server/auth.py:9 and src/payment.ts:17, (3) SQL injection in src/payment.ts:11. The legacy-monolith.js is an extreme example of copy-paste bloat with a logic bug (dead code branch) in every handler. Duplication between utils.js and helpers.js is verbatim. Dependency hygiene is poor (latest, *, duplicate lodash). No lockfile. Import cycle between a.js and b.js. Several files (orphan.js, payment.ts, lib/b.js) appear unimported. The 'secrets' findings are false positives — they are redacted placeholders in test fixtures.

findings.suggestion: Replace with `JSON.parse(text)` and validate the resulting structure (e.g., with zod or manual checks).
findings.benefit: Eliminates arbitrary code execution; adds actual runtime validation.
findings.risk: Low — JSON.parse is a drop-in replacement for valid JSON; invalid input will now throw instead of executing.

findings.title: Dead code branch in every legacy-monolith handler (if (!data) never true)
findings.description: data is assigned the result of `ROUTES[cacheKey] || { ... }`, which is always truthy (either cached object or a new object). The `if (!data)` block is therefore unreachable; the nested logic inside it (lines 9-19) never executes.
findings.suggestion: Remove the dead branch and the redundant nested checks, or fix the logic if the intent was to check cache presence before assignment.
findings.benefit: Eliminates confusing dead code; may reveal intended cache-miss behavior.
findings.risk: Low — the dead code is not executed; removing it changes no behavior.

findings.title: save_config leaks file handle (no context manager)
findings.description: If fh.write() raises an exception, fh.close() is never called, leaking the file descriptor. Should use `with open(path, 'w') as fh:`.
findings.snippet:
def save_config(path, data):
    fh = open(path, "w")
    fh.write(data)
    fh.close()
findings.suggestion: Rewrite with a context manager: `with open(path, 'w') as fh: fh.write(data)`
findings.benefit: Guarantees file closure even on error.
findings.risk: None — purely safer pattern.

findings.title: Dependency hygiene issues in package.json (3)
findings.description:
- **express** `latest`: production dependency pinned to "*" / "latest" — builds are non-reproducible
- **lodash** `*`: production dependency pinned to "*" / "latest" — builds are non-reproducible
- **lodash** `* / 4.17.21`: same package in dependencies and devDependencies
findings.suggestion: Pin exact versions (lockfiles for npm/cargo; `==` pins or constraints.txt for pip) and audit ranges deliberately when upgrading.
findings.benefit: Reproducible builds and no surprise breaking upgrades.
findings.risk: Low — pinning alone changes no runtime behavior.

findings.title: No lockfile committed next to package.json
findings.description: Without a lockfile, every `npm install` resolves fresh versions — CI, teammates, and production can drift apart silently.
findings.suggestion: Commit the lockfile matching your package manager (npm/yarn/pnpm) and install with `npm ci` in CI.
findings.benefit: Identical dependency trees everywhere; fewer "works on my machine" failures.
findings.risk: None — adding a lockfile is additive.

findings.benefit: Deterministic module initialization and clean layering.
findings.risk: Moderate — moving code between modules can shift initialization order; run the full test suite after.
